rules.justification: Fast mode against the bitwise default (D-122, D-123), demonstrator of the harness: the gradient kernel evaluates each entry sum_l U(i,l) B(j,l) as a chain of fused multiply-adds instead of rounded products summed by a halving tree; each gradient entry then differs by at most a few units of 2^-53 relative to sum_l |U(i,l) B(j,l)|. The explicit lumped-mass step of linear elasticity at 0.8 of the critical time step is stable, so a perturbation of the internal forces of relative size eps per step grows at most linearly with the number of steps; after 20 steps the nodal fields u, v, a, f_int differ by a few eps relative to their largest magnitude. The bound 1e-12 of max|field| (about 4500 eps) leaves a factor of about 400 over the measured differences and fails on a kernel error, which changes the fields at the 1e-3 level or more.
rules.evidence: akantu-solid tests/fast_mode_gradient.rs, 5x5x5 tetrahedra (750 elements), 20 steps, small strain and finite deformation, 2026-11-16 (aarch64): largest |fast - bitwise| / max|bitwise| 2.4e-15 (a), 1.8e-15 (v), 0.8e-15 (f_int), 0.3e-15 (u); 25-75 % of the entries bit-identical
